NFL DFS Wide Receiver Rankings: Week 9 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, November 8 · 11 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of November 3, 12:36 PM ET

Puka Nacua is the top-projected wide receiver on the Week 9 DraftKings main slate at 23.6 DraftKings points for $8,800, at Washington. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (19.5, $9,300) and Amon-Ra St. Brown (18.7, $8,100) are next.

Puka Nacua is also the top value at the position: 2.68 projected points per $1,000.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the November 3, 12:36 PM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Wide receivers to know in Week 9

Puka Nacua, LAR at WAS ($8,800)

Puka Nacua carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 23.6 DraftKings points at $8,800, the 3rd-highest on the entire main slate. That is 4.1 points clear of Jaxon Smith-Njigba. The model gives him 10.7 targets on 30.6 routes. The salary works out to 2.68 projected points per $1,000, 1st of 27 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Nacua averaged 23.6 points with a simulated floor of 9.8 and a ceiling of 49.2, and he holds 20% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. The Rams are a 5.5-point favorite on the road against Washington, with an implied team total of 26.5 in a game totaled at 47.5.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba, SEA vs ARI ($9,300)

Jaxon Smith-Njigba projects 2nd at the position with 19.5 DraftKings points at $9,300. The model gives him 8.6 targets on 24.7 routes. The salary works out to 2.09 projected points per $1,000, 14th of 27 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Smith-Njigba averaged 19.4 points with a simulated floor of 6.0 and a ceiling of 44.8, and he holds 8% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Seattle is a 10.5-point favorite at home against Arizona, with an implied team total of 26.5 in a game totaled at 42.5.

Amon-Ra St. Brown, DET at MIA ($8,100)

Amon-Ra St. Brown projects 3rd at the position with 18.7 DraftKings points at $8,100. The model gives him 9.3 targets on 29.7 routes. The salary works out to 2.30 projected points per $1,000, 3rd of 27 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Brown averaged 18.6 points with a simulated floor of 5.7 and a ceiling of 41.6, and he holds 15% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Detroit is a 7-point favorite on the road against Miami, with an implied team total of 28.75 in a game totaled at 50.5.

Value: Malik Washington, MIA vs DET ($4,700)

Malik Washington projects for 10.7 DraftKings points at $4,700, which works out to 2.28 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 27 wide receivers the model projects for 9 or more points. The model gives him 5.8 targets on 21.9 routes. Across 10,000 simulations Washington averaged 10.8 points with a simulated floor of 2.9 and a ceiling of 24.5, and he holds 8% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Miami is a 7-point underdog at home against Detroit, with an implied team total of 21.75 in a game totaled at 50.5.
